notes.risersFallers: Biggest risers in the hybrid view are undefeated or quality-win teams that computers like (BYU, Texas Tech, Utah, UCLA, Tennessee). Georgia and Texas fall relative to pure polls due to unranked/home losses despite predictive strength. AP has Miami #1, BYU #2, Ohio State #3, Notre Dame #4, Georgia #5. Grok elevates Ohio State (elite efficiency + quality win) over Miami and keeps Georgia higher than pure poll drop might suggest, while ranking BYU very high but not #2 purely on the ND win (predictive still trails the top). UCLA is ranked lower than AP (#9) because of schedule strength concerns relative to predictive models. Big 12 teams (BYU, Utah, Texas Tech, Houston) are well-represented and not penalized; the hybrid rewards their results and efficiency without brand inflation. Alabama and Texas sit lower than brand/predictive alone would suggest due to losses.

notes.nextWeek: Week 8 features Utah vs. Houston, BYU at UCF, LSU at Auburn, Miami vs. Pitt, Alabama vs. Texas A&M, and several Big Ten/SEC games (including USC and others). An upset in any Big 12 top matchup or an SEC loss for a borderline team (e.g., LSU/Auburn or Alabama) could reorder the 8–15 range and affect conference title odds. Ohio State and others have byes or lighter tests that could solidify top spots.
notes.cfpOutlook: Projected byes: Ohio State (Big Ten champ candidate), Miami (ACC champ), BYU (Big 12 champ candidate), Notre Dame or Georgia. Likely field includes Indiana, Texas Tech, Utah, UCLA/Tennessee, Ole Miss, Houston, and a G5 (Boise State or similar). Big Ten: Ohio State or Indiana leading; UCLA/Oregon in mix. SEC: Georgia still strong despite loss; Tennessee/Ole Miss rising. Big 12: BYU/Utah/Texas Tech all undefeated and viable champs. ACC: Miami clear favorite. Independents/G5: Notre Dame in at-large mix if it stays top-12; Boise State or James Madison leading G5 auto-bid path. Multiple 1- or 2-loss teams remain alive.
